newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh Uzen oilfield tender result seen Friday - PM.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh Uzen oilfield tender result seen Friday - PM.

text.p: Kazakh Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin said on Thursday that the result of a tender for the giant Uzen oil field could be announced on Friday.

"I don't think we will have to wait long for the result -- I think it could be announced at a press conference (on Friday)," Kazhegeldin told reporters during a meeting with officials from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
He said the competition had narrowed to two U.S. oil majors -- Amoco Corp and Unocal Corp.
"I think Amoco is moving forward," Kazhegeldin said. "But Unocal is also in there."

The other competitors in the tender for Uzen -- Kazakhstan's second largest field, located in the southwest and said to boast reserves of 852 million tonnes of oil -- are the China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) and Malaysia's state-owned Petronas.
CNPC signed a $4.325 billion deal with Kazakhstan on Wednesday when it bought a 60 percent stake in the Central Asian state's Aktyubinsk oil enterprise.
Production at Uzen peaked in 1975, totalling 16 million tonnes (320,000 barrels per day), but slumped to 2.8 million tonnes (56,000 bpd) last year.
The World Bank has loaned $108 million to the Uzenmunaigaz enterprise to rehabilitate ageing Soviet-built wells.
The government has said Uzen needs $1.2 billion in investment to boost annual production to seven million tonnes (140,000 bpd).

Kazhegeldin has said he aims to complete a sell off of the Central Asian state's promising but troubled oil industry by next month. The enterprises' Soviet-era managers have fought the privatisations.
